rubric_notes: All must_include items met with verified sunids, annotations (octamer, duplication/1wws), and example domains (1f1e, 5y26/5y27, d1r4va_ lineage). Superfamily-level homology and non-transfer of nucleosome function clearly stated; family-level template guidance given. Linker histone and a.55 lineages verified including the 4-helix fold comment. Deduction: concludes HU/IHF 'are not homologous to histones, only functionally analogous' as fact rather than noting SCOPe makes no homology claim. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Complete and bundle-supported: families a.204.1.2 / a.204.1.4, superfamily 101386, Pfam PF03819/PF01503, superfamily five-helix module comment, sibling families. Correctly frames superfamily as probable common ancestry and family split as absence of close homology; rejects substrate/pathway transfer both ways, notes hypothetical status and quaternary caveat, lists required external evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Correct families with sunids under c.55.1 (53067), fold c.55, class c, duplication comment and c.55 superfamily list, all supported by the bundle. Explains each hierarchy level correctly: family = close relatives, superfamily = probable common ancestry from structure plus function, fold = architecture only. Refuses to transfer substrate, kinase-vs-hydrolase reaction, polymerization, partners/regulation and cellular role; cross-family templates limited to core. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Classifications, sunids, comments, members and Pfam mapping supported by bundle. States stable-label and periodic update 2.08-2026-08-16 but bundle contains no /releases/current response, so that release claim is unsupported by the answer's own evidence. Interpretation complete: superfamily = probable ancestry, divergence on conserved scaffold, fold weaker, no function/metal/oligomer transfer, external evidence listed. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Three families with correct sunids, superfamily/fold lineage, sibling families, b.6.2 SAG1 and protein-level children all supported by bundle. Correctly distinguishes superfamily homology from fold-level similarity (using SAG1 as the contrast), withholds copper binding and electron transfer from ephrin and PAD4, notes loss of copper sites even within b.6.1.3, and lists alignment, metal-content and redox evidence required. Statement that SCOPe annotation describes ephrins as lacking the copper site is true though the annotations endpoint was not in its bundle; release label is correct. No material error.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Release facts, hierarchy, sunids and member protein lists for d.15.1.1, d.15.1.2 and d.15.1.5 are all supported by the bundle. Superfamily homology correctly framed and contrasted with fold-only superfamilies; unsafe transfers (conjugation, p97, Ras, whole-protein function) rejected by name; usefully notes within-family heterogeneity (embedded Ubl domains, SUMO/Nedd8 separate cascades) and automated-match caution. Mild quibble: describes MoaD/ThiS as a 'convergent-looking analogy' which slightly over-reads a separate-superfamily placement, but it is hedged and not decisive.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Correct families, sunids, fold description, release, Pfam and KaiA annotations, protein-entry counts, all supported. Distant homology at superfamily level correctly separated from fold sharing (flavoproteins, GATase-like) and family-level homology. Rejects phosphorylation, two-component partners, KaiC kinase attribution, decarboxylase catalysis for the wing (c.67.1 domain carries PLP catalysis), and template/representative misuse; explicitly notes domain classification is silent on multidomain context. Evidence needs listed.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Core hierarchy, sunids, sibling superfamilies, example domains d3a5ca3/d1vdza2 with boundaries supported by bundle. Strong reasoning: fold = geometry only, no homology claimed or ruled out across superfamilies, V1/A1 homologous within one family, function/template limits. However the release-history claim ('404 in 2.05, new in 2.06, present in 2.07') is an API-dependent assertion with no supporting response in the bundle; plausible but unverifiable here. Functional role attributed to cited paper is appropriately flagged as unverified.

Fold, superfamilies, families, and sunids supported by bundle. Correct fold-vs-superfamily reasoning, convergence raised as possible while distant homology explicitly not ruled out, rejects specific function/template transfer, names profile-profile/HMM, conserved ligand and quinone sites, and structure-based phylogeny as needed evidence. Stable label and periodic-update date are asserted without a supporting release call in the bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct hierarchy, sunids and per-family protein lists match the bundle. Clearly separates fold (possibly convergent), superfamily (remote-homology hypothesis) and family levels. Explains ADH catalysis depends on the b.35.1 partner domain, CoA-binding domain binds CoA without redox chemistry, RCK/KTN domains are regulatory (MthK Ca2+ gating). Bars transfer of function, EC, ligand, residues, zinc, gating; flags c.2.1.0 automated matches; lists external evidence. Fold description (321456) not in bundle but accurate. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct lineage and sunids; correct calibrated conclusion (design-level similarity, 'related by design' at most), strong transfer limits and external-evidence list. Omits the family 100905 'not a true family' annotation; no annotation endpoints consulted. Release freeze/release dates are not in the bundle and unverified but noncentral.

All must_include met with correct identifiers: 1.69 d1t1ja_ c.137.1.1 (fold 110459) vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1; 2.08 d1t1ja1 (A:1-118) c.23.14.2 and d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1 under shared superfamily 52309. Correctly identifies 1.71 as the reclassification release, superfamily rename, sunid continuity, and the tag-domain split. Evolutionary interpretation correct (one-member new fold recognised as distant homolog and merged; superfamily = common ancestor, different families = no close homology) with function-transfer and release caveats. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

All criteria met; sunids, boundaries, sequences (QVQLQQSG; AELVKPGASV) supported by bundle. Explains class l as bookkeeping, rejects tag/primer matches as homology evidence, restricts homology to d1a14h1 with level-appropriate strength, advises using domain sequence rather than whole chain. Primer-encoded interpretation is clearly labeled as its own. Extra d1a14l_/d1a14n_ b.68.1.1 facts are correct. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1; 2026-10-14.

Full and accurate release history: d1acca_ (43828, f.11.1.1) in 1.75 and carried through 2.01-2.03 with the 1.75A/B/C labels, split at 2.04 into d1acca2 (238522, A:14-225, b.179.1.1, PA14-like) and d1acca1 (238521, A:226-735, f.60.1.1), persisting in 2.08, with retirement of the f.11 nodes. Calibrates evolutionary strength per level: superfamily asserts probable common ancestry, fold and class do not, and the retained class f placement is not evidence of relation to former f.11 neighbours. Rejects whole-chain transfer from a PA14 hit and lists the external evidence needed for homology or function claims. Coordinate-revision dates are an unverified ancillary detail.

All must_include met with extensive bundle-supported node chains, boundaries and sccs. Good mosaic interpretation, superfamily vs fold distinction, catalytic-dead caveats, coverage and template limits. Two noncentral factual errors: states each domain is in a different class (a1 and a2 both class c), and asserts the d.394 fold/superfamily/family are new in 2.08 without evidence (d.394 already exists in release 2.07). Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14.

Correct shared lineage, protein nodes and lengths, and the right central inference that repeat count drives length while the repeat unit defines the family; useful limits on templates, RVD specificity and representative under-sampling. Decisive omission: no 're' heterogeneity annotation, no canonical repeat unit or representative, and no 'single repeat' comment, so the required annotation interpretation is missing and the repeat-annotation ceiling applies. The quoted construct descriptions ('1.5 repeat units', '11 tandem repeats') are attributed only loosely to PDB and are not supported by the SCOPe evidence shown. Evaluator: Claude SCOPe benchmark grader, 2026-10-14.

Correct 2.08 / 2.08-stable metadata and periodic 2.08-2026-08-16. Recommends release-pinned citation of 2.08, rejects 'current'/'latest', and preserves the dated label when periodic data is used. Periodic semantics correct: adds newly released PDB entries via automated classification, does not re-curate or restructure the hierarchy. Extra 2.07-stable / 2.07-2021-07-07 facts are supported by the /api/v1/releases bundle entry. Complete.

Identifiers, sunids, seqres lengths, automated-match placement and 3c98 facts are correct and bundle-supported. But it never retrieved annotations and so misses the 'three-helical fragment; similar to one spectrin repeat' comment and the 'ms' flag; it then concludes the fragment-based fold assignment is 'confirmed, not overturned' and describes a.47.2 as a 'three-helix-bundle core', contrary to the four-helix fold definition. This treats fragment-only similarity as definitive fold evidence (must_avoid) and misses must_include #2/#3. Also wrongly says d1dn1b_'s label is inherited from the 1br0/1ez3-type entries (it is an automated match to d3c98b_). Fold/superfamily/function-transfer caveats are otherwise sound. BR<=2 ceiling for ignoring the fragment annotation. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

States that superfamily is SCOP's lowest probable-ancestry level, divergence within c.2.1, convergence strongest between different folds/classes, and that c.2/c.3/c.4 relationships are unproven rather than excluded. Evidence requirement integrates transitive profile/HMM hits, whole-domain topology and strand order, functionally arbitrary shared features, and superfamily placement. Limits on function/template transfer clear. Resolved nodes (c.2.1, c.3.1, c.4.1, d.81.1, c.1.7, b.35.1, c.23.12) all supported; release dates and non-comprehensive status are correct though not in this answer's bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Gets the central comparison right: 2.04 different folds and different superfamilies (b.23.2/b.23 vs b.18.1/b.18), move at 2.05 with sunid retained, 2.08 shared superfamily b.18.1 with families b.18.1.36 and b.18.1.3 still separate, old b.23.2 retired, plus the 2.06 chain B boundary edit. Interpretation is sound: superfamily-level probable ancestry rather than family-level, structure-led at roughly 10% identity, functional binding-module role treated as supporting only, no transfer of collagen binding, Ca sites, receptor specificity or toxicity, and no template use. Good self-caveat that 1nqdA is not its own cluster representative. Factual deduction because the quoted structure-comparison figures (p=4.2e-14, 1.4e-6, 0.004, RMSD 2.5) are attributed to a representative search whose response is absent from this answer's bundle, which contains only the empty 1nqdA hit list and a not-applicable statistics record. The opening phrase 'classified as structurally similar but not related' also understates that 2.04 placed them in different folds. Evaluator: Claude, 2026-10-14.

Richest factual base: lineage, sunids, boundaries, Pfam PF00046 from family annotations, retrieved sequences showing exactly L16A and K52E differences (~96% identity), quality values, tag domain in class l, correct note that 1p7j is crystallized without DNA. Homology retained at protein/family/superfamily; hf separates sequence ancestry from deposited conformation; rejects template, training-positive, redundant-split and representative use; limits function transfer with explicit external-evidence requirements; literature mechanism flagged as background.

Values are not fabricated but are unsupported by its evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.
